note: 6ths, 7ths and the octave side by side: the three leaps from one Do over a drone, an octave-stage tune with an octave and a 6th sung with the tune and then over the chords alone, then a 7ths-stage tune alone and a cappella. The old Key choice is moves (key any, first in F) and its line opens with {{?key}}; the tunes' notes are degree tokens. Missing: an octave-stage tune that holds a 6th, a 7th and an octave together (no tune in the book has all three), so the last tune comes from the 7ths stage.

exercise.title: 6ths, 7ths and the octave, side by side
exercise.why: From Do, a 6th, a 7th and an octave land on three notes next to each other, La, Ti and the high Do, so a wide leap is in tune when you hear which of the three it lands on before you leave Do.

cells.heading: La, Ti or the high Do

cells.text:
Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together, and your pitch shows on the staff. From the low {{1}}, leap up to {{6}} and back, then up to {{7}} and back, then up to the next {{1}} and back. Sing it on "oo".
Then sing the three leaps in an order you make up, and hear the landing note before you leave {{1}}.
Practice until each leap lands without a slide.
{{?key}}In another key the drone moves, and {{7}} is still a half step under the high {{1}}.

Press Play below to hear the tune: the mic starts with it. It opens with an octave, from the {{5}} under {{1}} up to {{5}}, and in its second bar it leaps a 6th from {{3}} up to the high {{1}}. Listen once, then sing along. Sing it on "la".
Then press Tune below to mute the tune, and sing it over the chords alone.
If the 6th lands off, sing {{3}} and the high {{1}} alone, slowly, then put the leap back in the tune.

This tune leaps a 7th twice: from {{1}} up to {{7}} at the start, and from {{2}} up to the high {{1}} in the second bar. Press Play below to hear it alone, with no chords under it: the mic starts with it. Listen once, then sing along. Sing it on "la".
Then press Tune below to mute the tune, and sing it a cappella.
If a 7th lands on the octave, sing the octave on purpose, step down one note, then sing the leap again.
